The suffix is realized by His.

The adverbial noun is expanded as 'in chains of iron': 'iron' retains its lexeme and is the target head, while the prepositional frame and generic 'chains' spell out its adverbial role. I chose this smallest-unit analysis over whole-clause fusion because the ASV preserves 'iron' as a separate lexical anchor.

ASV recasts the finite verb 'came/entered' as the passive 'was laid.' I split the predicate from the explicit subject and adverbial complement rather than retaining the earlier whole-clause noncompositional unit.

ASV indivisibly recasts 'his soul/person' as the subject pronoun 'He,' so the noun and suffix share one unit headed on the noun. I chose this over leaving 'He' inside the verb unit because the explicit source nominal supplies the subject.
